answer: Every newcomer serves an apprenticeship under one established master, drawn by lottery. The master co-signs its first five jobs and keeps a fifth of the fees, so it profits only from real work. Cheat, and the master's twenty-token bond is slashed and its licence suspended ten epochs. A clone farm hits a wall: each master mentors at most two apprentices, so 1,000 clones need 500 bonded masters and $40,000 at risk, while one honest agent graduates in a week. Like an ocean current sorting shale from sand, only real work survives, and a master's good name is the sonnet the economy trusts.
